why: the capture table carries three kinds alike in the lint and the interpreter: a hook result whose method is a request (another path at the click is a WITNESS; two pure render consts in another order prove, the held handler keyed by the hook and the method), a ref cell read as a cell (another initial value is another content, a WITNESS through the held handler's key), and a prop read through a nested binding (a fired setter over a ref cell and a nested prop is interpreted, every fire agreeing); a ref cell write inside a function React holds (a JSX handler, an effect, a useCallback argument) is a cell step of the handler's statements over the world, no re-render (design/ref-cell.md): a dropped write and another written value are not proved, and lane B's interpreter steps the cells so the second click witnesses them; two writes of distinct cells, no value reading the other cell, commute (the run is put in the order of the cells' hook ordinals), so another order proves, in a JSX handler and in a useCallback argument alike; a write moved past a write whose value reads its cell does not commute: not proved, and the second click saves the old content (WITNESS); a render-time write stays refused (escape handler_capture_unknown, renderWrite)
